requirements.title: Customer Authentication and Device Binding
requirements.text: Customer Authentication and Device Binding. The system must authenticate retail banking customers using a customer identifier and a passcode validated against a salted hash, and must issue a signed JWT access token with a configurable expiry. Every successful authentication response must return a unique session_id and a device_binding_id that ties the session to a registered device fingerprint, enabling session revocation, device de-registration, and a complete audit trail of access events.

requirements.title: Account Balance and Statement Retrieval
requirements.text: Account Balance and Statement Retrieval. The system must expose authenticated endpoints to list all accounts owned by the customer and to retrieve a paginated transaction statement for a single account. Each account record must include account_id, account_type, currency, available_balance, and ledger_balance. Statement retrieval must accept from_date, to_date, page, and page_size parameters, and each transaction line must carry transaction_id, posting_date, description, amount, and running_balance.

requirements.title: Beneficiary Management
requirements.text: Beneficiary Management. The system must allow authenticated customers to list, register, and delete payment beneficiaries. Registering a beneficiary requires beneficiary_name, account_number, and ifsc_code, and the response must return a server-assigned beneficiary_id together with an activation_status field. Newly added beneficiaries must remain in a cooling_period state and must not be usable as a transfer destination until the cooling period has elapsed.

requirements.title: Fund Transfer Idempotency
requirements.text: Fund Transfer Idempotency. Every fund transfer request must carry a unique, client-provided idempotency_key in the request body so that a retried or duplicated submission is processed exactly once. The idempotency_key must be echoed back in the transfer confirmation response alongside the transfer_id, giving the client end-to-end proof that a retry did not create a second debit. A transfer request submitted without an idempotency_key must be rejected with a structured validation error.

requirements.title: Standing Instructions and Scheduled Payments
requirements.text: Standing Instructions and Scheduled Payments. The system must allow customers to create recurring standing instructions specifying a source account, a registered beneficiary, an amount, a frequency (daily, weekly, monthly), a start_date, and an optional end_date. The response must return an instruction_id and the computed next_execution_date. Standing instructions must be cancellable by the customer at any time before the next execution.

requirements.title: Debit Card Controls
requirements.text: Debit Card Controls. Authenticated customers must be able to modify the security controls on any card they own through a dedicated endpoint. Controllable attributes must include a freeze flag to instantly block the card, per_transaction_limit, daily_limit, and boolean toggles for international_usage, online_usage, and contactless_usage. The response must confirm the resulting control state for every attribute.

requirements.title: Step-Up Authentication for High-Value Transfers
requirements.text: Step-Up Authentication for High-Value Transfers. All high-value operations — defined as a transfer exceeding 50,000 in account currency, or the first payment to a newly registered beneficiary — must require step-up authentication before the operation is permitted to proceed. The system must expose a dedicated step-up challenge endpoint that issues a time-limited one-time passcode to the customer's registered channel, and a step-up verify endpoint that validates the submitted code and returns a short-lived step_up_token before the primary operation is authorised.

requirements.title: Transaction Dispute and Chargeback Filing
requirements.text: Transaction Dispute and Chargeback Filing. The system must allow customers to raise a dispute against a settled transaction and to track its resolution. Filing a dispute requires the transaction_id, a dispute_reason drawn from a controlled vocabulary (fraudulent, duplicate_charge, service_not_received, incorrect_amount), and an optional free-text narrative. The system must return a dispute_id, a provisional_credit_status, and an expected_resolution_date, and must expose a retrieval endpoint returning the current dispute status and its full event timeline.
